about.purpose: Machine-readable index of this GitHub account. Written for AI assistants (any vendor) and for people arriving cold, so neither has to infer the layout from repo names.
about.subject: Flat-to-VR game modding: converting existing flat PC games to VR, plus the reusable knowledge produced along the way.
about.stated_goal: The playable VR mods matter, but the durable goal is the knowledge, published so others can reuse it.
about.layout_change: 2026-08-30: consolidated from six repos per game (101 repos) to ONE public repo per game plus one private staging monorepo (22 repos). Each former repo is now a folder inside its game repo, with full git history preserved behind a subtree join commit.

headline: 2026-09-14: two cameras found in one day. Dead Space 2's projection is at constant register c4 and Prototype's at c0, both left-handed, both read live through a d3d9 proxy built, self-tested and deployed the same day. Six of the eight projects started on 2026-09-13 were advanced; four of them by static reading alone. The day also produced two corrections to this file's own earlier claims and one account-wide latent bug found in three other projects' proxies.

read_first.if: You are about to drive or automate one of these games
read_first.why: Keys, menu routes, state detection and entry points, per game. Vendor-neutral. Its UNIVERSAL.md carries the method rules that prevent the most wasted work.

read_first.if: You are doing reverse-engineering or VR conversion work
read_first.why: The engine-agnostic PLAYBOOK, the tool catalogue, and tools/ (small utilities that already earned their place).

read_first.if: You want what is known about an engine family
read_first.why: Cross-engine library. docs/engines/ has one page per engine family.

read_first.if: You are resuming work on a specific game
read_first.read: that game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md, then its modding-notes/ folder
read_first.why: The dossier is distilled current truth for that engine, including dead ends. The notes are the chronological ledger.

mod/.holds: release packaging and player-facing docs; the releases themselves are GitHub Releases on the game repo
mod/.note: Often sparse. A project with no release yet has a near-empty mod/; this is expected, not a mistake.

dev-archive/.holds: the live working mod source AND the messy dev history: snapshots, probes, recon evidence, dead ends
dev-archive/.note: This is where the actual mod source lives, commonly under dev-archive/tools/.

modding-notes/.holds: readable field notes and the dated progress ledger

engine-research/.holds: ENGINE-DOSSIER.md — distilled truth about that game's engine, including a dead-ends section

external-research/.holds: leads gathered from public sources by a research-only session; INDEX.md plus topics/

staging.holds: unverified work-in-progress for every project, one folder per game (staging/<prefix>/); the cross-machine handoff channel

conventions.history_note: Each folder was its own repo until 2026-08-30. Full per-file history is preserved and reachable through the folder's subtree join commit (git log the merge parents). The old <prefix>-<suffix> repo names redirect only where a repo was renamed (each game's -mod became the game repo).

session_lanes.note: Five kinds of session, each typed as a slash-command. They are designed to run at the same time; one_writer_per_file below is what keeps them from colliding.

lanes./lm (live modding): the only lane that may launch a game, attach a debugger or drive VR
lanes./pd (parallel development): advances every project as far as it can with no game running
lanes./gr (game research): public-research sweep; curates each game repo external-research/
lanes./gs (github sweep): read-only hygiene audit of the whole estate; curates nothing

background_agents.never_in_includes: the standing /gate-watch background watcher, which is otherwise permitted everywhere (owner ruling, 2026-09-03): those two lanes run fully inline.
background_agents.rationale: The three sweep lanes are breadth-first over many projects and leave their output as reviewable commits. /lm drives a live game, which no agent may do. /gs is an audit whose value is that the session performed each check itself, so a second-hand summary would defeat it.
background_agents.still_applies: Even where allowed, agents must be few and each must have a job the owner could name without asking; ad-hoc fan-out is not the intent.

one_writer_per_file.rule: Every file has exactly one kind of session that may edit it. Reading is unrestricted.

lanes.modding: curates mod/, dev-archive/, modding-notes/, engine-research/ and the staging repo

one_writer_per_file.cross_lane: Contributions travel as new, uniquely-named files dropped in the receiving lane's inbox/ folder — never as edits to a file another lane curates.

meta_repos.name: lanes-plugin
meta_repos.purpose: A collection of tools for flat-to-VR AI modding with Claude: skills, helper programs and checks for Claude Code that take a flat-screen PC game into VR, from the first look inside the game to the build you wear in the headset. The Claude Code plugin these projects are worked with: named session lanes, a shared work board, claim guards, a naming rule that keeps personal names out of everything written, and an ideas inbox that sessions file automatically. Early version (public since 2026-09-24), still being built.

meta_repos.name: BeG0nE
meta_repos.purpose: BeG0nE: tools and mods that remove unwanted features and faults from video games, one folder per cure, each a toolkit for modders plus drop-in fixes per game. Occlusion Drift BeG0nE (VR two-handed weapons held with the left controller above the right, so tracking never drops; first game RE Village on REFramework) and Camera Jitter/Shake BeG0nE (the stepped camera common in AI-written VR mods; first find out why).

meta_repos.name: vr-bench
meta_repos.purpose: VR Bench: an OpenXR API layer that plays both VR controllers (poses, buttons, sticks) from a JSON file, so a VR game can be tested and learned on the OpenXR Simulator with nobody in the headset. Driven by /lanes:bench in the Lanes plugin.

meta_repos.name: blender-cubekit
meta_repos.purpose: Pixel-style cube (voxel) models for games, built in Blender by script: one cube size per project, named settings, pick any cube, stop-motion animation, game export. Scripts, a Blender add-on and tutorials. Framework only; game models live in their own project folders.

meta_repos.name: animation-timing-vr
meta_repos.purpose: A desktop window plus one REFramework script: freeze, step, slow down and nudge the player's animations in RE Engine games, with keys per frame; with Visceral RE8 it holds the mod's finger movements on a frame, adds or removes frames, moves the whole hand on the gun and tunes the mod's named timings live. Sister of Hand Poser.

notes_for_ai_readers: Folder presence varies: a missing folder means that stage has not been reached yet.
Prefer ai-game-control-profiles over inferring controls from these repos — the game repos describe how a game was MODIFIED, not how to OPERATE it.
Every game repo's engine-research/ENGINE-DOSSIER.md has a dead-ends section. Read it before proposing an approach; several plausible-looking routes have already been tried and refuted.
Claims in the notes carry dates. Where a later entry contradicts an earlier one, the later entry wins and usually says so explicitly.
